instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Five starts — injury and a falling-out with Roy Evans, not a drop in ability.
Recalled by England for Euro 96 at 31; the best of his Liverpool seasons.
Joined Manchester City in March 1994.
Bradford’s main creative outlet in a survival season, at 33; still an honest lower-half winger.
Thirty-four, nine starts, and relegation with Bradford; the crossing was still the only thing about him above the level.
Thirty-nine and an ever-present for a Forest side that conceded 69; a competent shot-stopper a long way below modern standard.
A fractured skull in 1996 and a chronic knee problem; a bit-part player at 35.
In and out of the side after injury and a change of manager; the ability was unchanged.
Three years at Celtic in between, including a Scottish Player of the Year award; he came back a better midfielder.
Eleven starts and relegation with Derby at 29; the last of his top-flight football.
Ever-present and the most consistent defender at the club that season; the ceiling was still a good lower-half left-back.
Nineteen and an ever-present in central midfield; enormous energy and ball-winning, almost nothing on the ball.
An ever-present in Reading’s seventh-placed first season and capped by England; the left foot did all of it.
Enormous and genuinely dominant in the air, and by Stoke a first-choice Premier League centre-half; the lack of pace was always the way past him.
A near ever-present at 22 and called up by England; dominant in the air, limited on the turn.
Thirty-six years old and a first-choice centre-half for a promoted side; reading and positioning entirely compensating for the pace that had gone.
Six years on from QPR, two of them outside the top flight; a durable, limited left-back who was a slightly better player at 31 than at 25.
Back in England at 33 after three seasons at Helsingborg; the reading and the technique survived, the pace did not.
Seventeen, thrown in at centre-half, and physically already a Premier League player.
Excellent alongside Stam in the treble season; a genuinely good centre-half whose career was cut short by injury rather than a limit of ability.
Eleven starts; the knee trouble that eventually forced him out of Manchester United had begun to cost him whole months.
A season at Barcelona in between; back in England at 30 as a good, aggressive holding midfielder rather than the passer who had won a Double and a World Cup.
Technically the best player in a mid-table Sunderland side at 19; later an Olympic gold medallist with Argentina. Rated on ability, not on Sunderland’s league position.
Technically the best midfielder in a Forest side that finished third; a genuine goal threat from deep.
Sixteen league goals from the wing; genuinely one of the most dangerous wide players in Europe that season.
Sharp fall in output and influence before the Fiorentina move; the level dropped with it.

Four years, Fiorentina and Rangers on from Everton, and on loan at a relegated Manchester City at 31; seven starts, no goals, and none of the directness that made him an 86. The eight-point fall is spread across four seasons away.
The reigning Champions League winner, and when fit the best defender in the record-breaking Chelsea back line — quick, aggressive in the tackle and a superb reader of a through ball.
The best defender in a back four that conceded 24; reading and recovery a clear level above the partner who got the headlines.
PFA Team of the Year in his first English season; defensively excellent and already an international-class right back.
Thirty-five starts in a Liverpool side that finished second conceding thirty; shot-stopping and reflexes of a clearly elite standard in his first English season.
The season of the Old Trafford errors and the confidence that went with them; the raw ability was unchanged, the reliability that is part of a goalkeeper’s ability was not.
Five starts, the place gone to Reina, and thirty-two years old; competent when called on and no longer a first choice anywhere.
On loan and central to the Great Escape; left foot, pace and a genuine top-flight athlete at nineteen.
Age 37, seven starts for a relegated Wednesday; a long way past his level.
Regular left-back in the Ipswich side that finished fifth; his best season.
The Birmingham loan: an ever-present, PFA Team of the Year, and the season he went from promising to England’s first choice.
Eighteen clean sheets, the Golden Glove and the PFA team of the year in his first season as City first choice.
A miserable season at Spurs with no league goals, but a forward who had scored heavily below and became a genuinely good Premier League centre-forward later. Rated between the two.
Two league goals in thirty-two starts, but the hold-up play and the link were the reason he started every week.
His best season: eight goals, a Europa League run led from the front, and an England call-up at twenty-nine.
A broken leg in September; nine starts, and five goals in them.
